column1: # Which suites a changed path can affect: <zsh glob><TAB><selectors>. scripts/test-select.sh reads
# this table; scripts/test-test-select.sh pins it. A path takes the union of every row it matches,
# and a path no row matches selects `everything`, so a new kind of file errs towards running more.
# `*` crosses `/`, so `*.md` is markdown at any depth and `daemon/*` everything under daemon/.
# Selectors: everything, toolchain, daemon, target:<Target>, suite:<Target>.<Suite>, none
# (`none` is for paths no test reads; it adds nothing, so a path that only matches it runs nothing).
# A row is here because a test reads the path, so the cross-reads are rows too: the wire fixtures
# and the daemon's delivery module are read by Swift suites, the hooks by the status line shim's
# tests, the Info.plist by the release feed's. Keep a new reader in step with its row here.
# OperatorEvalTests reads daemon/aitermd and daemon/tools but is opt-in and spends quota, so no
# scripts/test-test-select.sh fails when a test reads outside its own target and is not accounted for
# here, so a new cross-read cannot fall out of the routing unnoticed. It looks for Swift files that
# use `#file` or `#filePath` and daemon tests that climb out of daemon/. A Swift reader is accounted for by a
# `suite:<Target>.<File>` on a row above, or by its name on a `# reads only its own target:` or
# `# opt-in, reads outside its target:` line; a daemon reader by `<test file>=<path it reads>` on the
# `# daemon readers outside daemon/:` line, where a row above must route that path to daemon.
# Add the name when a new test only reads its own target's files; add a row when it reads another's.
# reads only its own target: PaletteDistinctionTests OperatorPlanToolsTests OperatorWakerTests OperatorCommandTests OperatorCurrentContractTests
# opt-in, reads outside its target: OperatorEvalTests
# The daemon, and what the Swift suites read from it.
# Swift sources: each target is built into the ones above it, and the test support is shared.
# The manifest is the toolchain guard's too: it loads it with the pinned Swift and fails on a warning.
# The toolchain and the test runner themselves: a change here can break any suite.
# The build scripts the toolchain guard's fixtures run: check-bundle-verifier.sh runs the bundle
# verifier, and check-build-scripts.sh runs snapshots.sh and make-app.sh, which both run build-app.sh.
# The release and picture scripts, which only a person runs; the fixtures copy them but never run them.
